verdict: FAIL on schema-invalid snapshot; otherwise scoped rendering checks PASS

findings.title: The control UI converts a schema-invalid HTTP 200 response into a healthy empty state
findings.confidence: high for the client behavior; production occurrence not established

source.details: Missing daemon data becomes database ok; missing arrays become empty lists.
Any syntactically valid JSON HTTP 200 snapshot clears the error state.

preconditions: Control UI loads the audited static assets.
Its summary endpoint returns HTTP 200 application/json with {}.
Browser polling fallback is active in the observed fixture.
reproduction: Run fixtures/browser/qa/run-control-browser.js using Playwright MCP browser_run_code_unsafe code argument.
findings.expected: An incomplete snapshot is reported as unavailable or invalid, without inventing a healthy database or absence of projects.
findings.observed: The page displays 'En direct', 'v— · base ok', '0 projet actif, 0 intervention attendue.', shows the empty welcome state and hides the error.
findings.impact: A malformed/contract-incompatible response can reassure the operator that there are no interventions. This observation concerns UI presentation only: it is not a Supervisor audit verdict PASS and does not establish a gate bypass.
findings.minimal_recommendation: Validate the snapshot envelope and required daemon status/collection fields before applying defensive display defaults; route failures through the existing error state.
findings.correction_test: Return HTTP 200 {} and assert the error is visible, database health is unknown, the empty-project success state is not shown, and a later valid snapshot recovers.
findings.limits: Response shape was fault-injected by a mock route. No evidence that the current real server emits this response.
